body.statement: If \(\lambda_K\to\infty\), then uniformly over \((\theta_{dj})\in\mathcal T_K(r)\), \(\sqrt{\lambda_K}(\widehat L_K-L_K)/\sqrt{\widehat V_K}\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1)\) and \(\widehat V_K-V(\rho_K)\to0\) in probability. The unprojected Wald interval \([\widehat L_K\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_K/\lambda_K}]\) has uniform coverage \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) for \(L_K\).
body.justification: This theorem identifies the transition from finite non-Gaussian information to ordinary studentized inference without changing the finite-array target.
body.gap: Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn's Proposition~3.2 gives the key smooth-density estimation bound, Proposition~3.3 gives the quadratic-objective stability inequality, and Theorem~3.2 gives the resulting central limit theorem; none covers binary marks or deterministic collision sampling.
body.consumer: Once the estimated collision intensity is large, practitioners can replace certified Poisson decisions by a simple variance-matched Wald procedure.
body.proof_tex:
First note consequences of the sparse assumptions that will be used in divisions and limits.  Since the arm sizes are positive integers,
\[
 \varepsilon_K=\frac{n_0n_1(n_0+n_1)}{K^2}
 \ge\frac{n_d^2}{K^2}\quad(d=0,1).
\]
Thus \(n_d/K\to0\).  Moreover
\[
 \frac{\lambda_K^2/K}{\varepsilon_K}
 =\frac{n_0n_1}{K(n_0+n_1)}
 \le\frac{\min(n_0,n_1)}K\longrightarrow0,
\]
so \(\lambda_K^2/K\to0\).  The deterministic comparison error \(d_K\) therefore tends to zero.

In \(\mathcal E_{\lambda_K,\rho}\), conditional on \(N=m\), the marks are independent with
\[
 \mu_\rho=\mathbb ES_\ell=c\rho,qquad
 \sigma_\rho^2=1-c^2\rho^2\ge1-c^2r^2>0. \tag{18}
\]
The strict lower bound follows from \(a,b<1/2\), hence \(c<1\), and \(r<1\).  The elementary characteristic-function expansion for bounded centered marks is uniform for \(\rho\in[-r,r]\): for fixed \(t\),
\[
 \mathbb E_\rho\exp\left\{
 it\frac{S-\mu_\rho}{\sigma_\rho\sqrt m}
 \right\}
 =1-\frac{t^2}{2m}+O(m^{-3/2}),
\]
where the remainder is uniform by (18).  Raising to the \(m\)-th power proves the uniform conditional central limit theorem.  Also \(N/\lambda_K\to1\) in probability because
\[
 \Pr\{|N/\lambda_K-1|>\epsilon\}
 \le\frac1{\epsilon^2\lambda_K},
\]
uniformly because the count law is parameter free, and \(\Pr(N=0)=e^{-\lambda_K}\to0\).  On \(N>0\), factor the studentized quantity as
\[
 \frac{\sqrt N(\overline S-c\rho)}{\sigma_\rho}\,
 \sqrt{\frac{\lambda_K}{N}}\,
 \frac{\sigma_\rho}{\sqrt{1-\overline S^2+N^{-1}}}.
\]
The first factor has the uniform conditional Gaussian limit, and the last two converge uniformly in probability to one.  Therefore
\[
 \frac{\sqrt{\lambda_K}(\overline S-c\rho)}
 {\sqrt{1-\overline S^2+N^{-1}}}
 \rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,1),
 \qquad
 \overline S-c\rho\to0
\]
uniformly in \(\rho\in[-r,r]\).  Since \(c=4ab\),
\[
 \widehat L_K-(a-b\rho)
 =-\frac{\overline S-c\rho}{4a},
 \qquad
 \widehat V_K- V(\rho)
 =\frac{-\overline S^2+c^2\rho^2+N^{-1}}{16a^2}. \tag{19}
\]
Equations (18)--(19) prove the asserted studentized limit and variance consistency in the marked experiment.  On \(N=0\), the declared fixed positive default makes the quotient well defined, and this event is harmless because its probability is \(e^{-\lambda_K}\to0\).

For every deterministic array, the collision statistic has total-variation distance at most \(d_K\to0\) from this marked experiment at \(\rho=\rho_K\).  Total variation controls every event, so the convergence in (19), its uniformity, and variance consistency transfer without any moment argument.  Substituting the standard-normal quantile in the transferred studentized convergence yields
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\mathcal T_K(r)}
 \Pr_\theta\left\{
 L_K\in\left[\widehat L_K\pm z_{1-\alpha/2}
 \sqrt{\widehat V_K/\lambda_K}\right]
 \right\}=1-\alpha+o(1).
\]
No projection is used, so there is no boundary atom.  This is a random-count characteristic-function argument followed by a uniform total-variation transfer.
